_instructions: Phase A of E0a: the understanding of a gathering turn of slot filling (LLMDialogClient.extract_turn), asked as slot_filling.update asks it.

Fields: task, domain (the context of the request), slot_schema (the frame_schema_json format), frame_filled (the values already in the frame), unanswered (optional: slots left blank), history (the conversation so far; it ends with the robot's question), user_text, expected_act (values | question | skip | repeat | other, as defined in the extract_slots prompt), expected_extractions ([{slot, value}], canonical values, ints as numbers, list operations as {"_remove"|"_replace": true, "items": [...]}; empty unless the act is values).

A value of a slot ALREADY FILLED mentioned without a correction signal is not extracted. A value outside the canonical values of its slot is dropped by the code: such cases are not used (their act would be ambiguous).

Traps: bare values that look like nothing ("It's Laura"), values given with hesitation, indirect skips, questions that name a valid value, oddly phrased requests to repeat, mentions of a filled value, numbers outside the slot's allowed range (extracted as said: the code rejects them and the reply says the range).

Each case: id, language (en | es), description (English), category (the kind of case), trap (a case built to provoke the error the question must not make), origin (optional: the case of the student's Spanish dataset it reuses or translates).
No case may reuse content of an evaluation scenario (evaluation/experiments/scenarios) nor of the examples of config/prompts.yaml; check with: python3 -m core.dataset_check.
The expected values are decided by a person; a case a careful annotator could label otherwise is dropped, not kept.
